name: Development Handbook
one_liner: How this team works — the Project Handbook's development extension.
purpose: The Development Handbook documents the selected approach for developing the information system and how the domain-specific aspect of the project relates to the overall project level. It is an extension of the Project Handbook and must be aligned with the key controlling processes, project policies, rules and management approach described there — it is identified as a separate artefact but need not be a separate information carrier. Together with the Development Work Plan it forms the basis for managing the project's development activities, and it is a living document that absorbs whatever Iteration Reviews and Retrospectives change.

fields.what: Documents the approach chosen for developing the information system as part of the overall solution.
fields.pollux: Two-week iterations, quarterly releases, continuous delivery pipeline into pre-production.

fields.what: How the domain-specific aspect of the project relates to the overall project — the bridge to the managing layer.
fields.pollux: Iteration Review outputs feed the monthly Project Status Report; gates stay at project level.

fields.what: An extension aligned with the Project Handbook's key controlling processes, policies, rules and management approach.
fields.pollux: POLLUX keeps one container: the Development Handbook is an annex to the Project Handbook.

fields.what: Identified as a separate artefact but need not be a separate document; a single container and synchronised configuration management are allowed.
fields.pollux: Gantt (PSO) maintains both under one configuration item so versions cannot diverge.

fields.what: Documents any deviation from the standard PM²-Agile roles and from the standard RASCI table.
fields.pollux: Eiffel, seconded, may act as TeCo for one iteration when Lovelace is absent.

fields.what: The A-PCT adds roles to the PM² organisation; some reorganise existing PM² roles' responsibilities, and this must be clear.
fields.pollux: Curie (PrOw) now prioritises what CASTOR's Business Manager alone used to decide.

fields.what: Ensures domain-specific information reaches the PM² management plans — for example, risks needing visibility at project level.
fields.pollux: Architecture risks are logged in the agile layer and escalated to the project Risk Log weekly.

fields.what: Agile planning uses a completely different requirements approach: stories are the working units that drive progress.
fields.pollux: Stories replace the CASTOR requirements specification; acceptance criteria attach to each story.

fields.what: Because agile favours stakeholder collaboration over contract negotiation, the change process must be adjusted to reflect that agility.
fields.pollux: Re-prioritising the WIL is not a change request; moving a gate or the budget is.

fields.what: Describe clearly how progress is measured, since agile planning differs in essence from traditional approaches.
fields.pollux: Progress measured as delivered story points and completed features, never as documents produced.

fields.what: Identifies which agile artefacts will be used and records tailoring — including the tools implementing the Development Work Plan.
fields.pollux: WIL, Release Plan and Iteration Plans all live in one tool; no separate documents produced.

fields.what: PM²-Agile introduces the Coordinate–Implement–Review rhythm, letting standard phase boundaries overlap and become more flexible.
fields.pollux: Planning-phase work continued into iteration 1 while the Release 1 scope was still settling.

fields.what: Which tools and techniques the team uses, from estimating to reviews, and the level of formality of each review.
fields.pollux: Planning poker for relative estimates; Definition of Done includes accessibility and a data-protection check.

fields.what: Why PM²-Agile was tailored this way, so the deviation is a decision on record and not drift.
fields.pollux: Iterations fixed at two weeks to match SC2's promise of a new report view per iteration.

fields.what: Changes or improvements coming out of Iteration Retrospectives or Reviews are documented here as they happen.
fields.pollux: After retro 6 the Definition of Done gained the data-protection check that had been silently skipped.

fields.what: In Closing it is an essential point of reference for the project-end review meeting, then properly closed and archived.
fields.pollux: Handbook v9 plus the Retrospectives Log form the input to the POLLUX project-end review.

fields.what: BM I · PM A · TeCo R · PrOw S · ArOw S · ATeM S — the guide's own worked RASCI example (p.66).
fields.pollux: Lovelace writes it; Curie, Einstein and the developers support; Hopper is informed when it is complete.

traps: Development Handbook extends the Project Handbook — it does not replace it.
It is created in Planning, not Initiating like the governance artefacts.
Handbook = how the team works; Development Work Plan = what and when.
TeCo is Responsible, not the PM — the PM is Accountable.
Separate artefact does not mean separate document: one carrier is allowed.
